# ModDotPlot Browser design reference

**Note:** This file was generated by ChatGPT 5.6 Sol under the direction of Adam Phillippy.

This is the authoritative engineering design. The narrower
[scientific specification](SCIENTIFIC_SPEC.md) is normative for numeric behavior;
[ADR 0004](adr/0004-validated-production-backend.md) records how the current backend
was selected.

## 1. Product requirements

ModDotPlot Browser is a static, install-free desktop web application for interactive
self, pairwise, and bounded multi-sequence grid genomic dotplots.

Required behavior:

1. Stage one or more FASTA records, optional matching FAI/GZI indexes, and optional
   annotations locally on separate launch targets, with a one-billion-base record
   bound; begin plotting only after the user explicitly selects **Explore**.
2. Select any record independently for each axis; self comparison is not a separate
   scientific code path.
3. Offer Self, Pairwise, and a serial six-sequence Grid mode for multi-record input,
   defaulting each newly loaded multi-record session to Self; retain a completed grid
   only while its cell-detail return flow is active.
4. Show a recognizable overview as early as possible, then improve it without blocking
   pan or zoom.
5. Preserve ModDotPlot maximum-containment semantics and display `ANI_c=C^(1/k)`,
   without treating `ANI_c` as biological average nucleotide identity.
6. Distinguish forward and reverse matches with evidence-aware color confidence.
7. Generate higher-resolution matrix tiles on demand, cache reusable work, prefetch a
   one-tile halo, and reach exact k-mer resolution.
8. Present Spectral and Viridis first, followed by the remaining ColorBrewer families,
   with palette-appropriate color-count bounds, reversible direction, and editable
   discrete colors. Use reversed 11-color Spectral on white as the initial plot style.
9. Keep sequence data inside the browser and make method provenance
   available for reproducible figures.
10. Prefer scientific correctness over throughput, then optimize within the validated
    estimator contract.
11. Let the bundled example publish its common default view from a small, reproducible
    precomputed artifact without weakening scientific configuration or source
    provenance checks; fetch raw sequence ranges and annotations only when needed.

No mobile support or session persistence is required in the current scope. Numeric
tiles are deliberately renderer-independent; export does not change the estimator.

## 2. System architecture

```text
precomputed overview artifact ── exact schema/config checks ──┐
FASTA streams or indexed record ranges ◀── FAI/GZI metadata ──┤
                                                              ▼
compute Web Worker ── Wasm ComputeSession ── PackedSequence
      │                      │
      │                      ├─ BuildSketch (temporary full OPH/HLL)
      │                      ├─ FrozenAxis (retained bit planes/scalars)
      │                      └─ bounded zoom-axis cache
      │
      ├─ transferable numeric MatrixTile channels
      ▼
main thread ── immutable renderer tile cache ── WebGL2 canvas
      │
      ├─ viewport/axes/controls/provenance
      └─ BEDPE/CSV and full-composition PNG/SVG/PDF export
```

The main thread owns interaction and rendering only. FASTA parsing, index validation,
indexed record selection, sketch construction, matrix comparison, and gzip/BGZF
decompression run in a worker. The site has
no runtime API, CDN dependency, telemetry, or analytics.

### Core crate

`moddotplot-core` is browser-independent and dependency-free. Its maintained surface is:

* packed DNA and streaming FASTA parsing;
* canonical ntHash2;
* undensified OPH and HLL;
* compact bit-sliced signatures and containment conversion;
* exact canonical k-mer sets used only as the scientific oracle;
* exact terminal k-mer tiles;
* axis construction, frozen summaries, and numeric tiles;
* immutable validated scientific configuration.

Rejected production candidates are not used by the browser. Git tag `v0.1.0` preserves
the old Phase 0/minmer/MashMap-compatible code when historical inspection is needed.
Candidate estimators, fused projection, sparse policy, and sparse kernels remain
available only through the non-default Rust `validation` module. The browser
distribution does not compile that feature or expose sparse correction.

### Wasm crate

`moddotplot-wasm` exposes a narrow stateful API:

* incremental FASTA transactions;
* scientific configuration metadata and digest;
* chunked, cancellable overview preparation;
* overview, zoom, and terminal tile requests;
* resource admission and memory estimates;
* consuming tile-channel transfer methods.

Preparation, exact cache identity, resource admission, composition state, and immutable
session selection context have separate ownership modules behind the thin binding.
It owns sequences and scientific caches. JavaScript never receives raw sequence bytes
except short base-code spans needed for exact terminal coloring.

### Browser application

The compute worker serializes state mutations and transfers owned typed arrays. Loaded
datasets, comparisons, and feature-track requests have separate immutable job IDs,
cancellation signals, configuration ownership, and publication guards. The renderer
retains CPU arrays for hover, context restoration, and cache fallback, plus one GPU
texture per tile channel.

The eager path streams every selected sequence file transactionally. The indexed path
accepts plain FASTA with FAI or BGZF FASTA with FAI and GZI, publishes validated record
metadata before sequence packing, and keeps browser `File` references for bounded
on-demand record reads. A global metadata index maps to the local Wasm sequence index
once that record is loaded. Ordinary gzip and incomplete companion sets use eager
loading; unmatched index files fail preflight.

The bundled-example fast path is separate from user-selected input. It first decodes a
small gzip-compressed artifact containing complete refined numeric tiles for the default
Chr1 self overview, all FAI sequence metadata, source-asset hashes, and the generating
scientific configuration. The loader first verifies the compressed bytes against a
pinned SHA-256 and requires the separately served FAI to equal the embedded index.
The worker accepts those tiles only when their full canonical
configuration identity and digest match a configuration constructed by the current
Wasm build. The raw bundled FASTA is represented by a same-origin, range-backed Blob;
it is not fetched in full before the default plot and supplies indexed record bytes only
when a later request cannot be served from precomputed or runtime caches. Bundled
annotation retrieval and parsing run as a separate post-workspace job and do not gate
the initial tiles.

## 3. Data representations

### PackedSequence

Two bits store each base and a sparse invalid-base bit vector distinguishes `A/C/G/T/U` from ambiguity
or gaps. `U/u` is normalized to `T/t`. Coordinates remain `u64`; no normalization may
shift them. FASTA is parsed incrementally and records are committed transactionally.
Eager and indexed ranges pass through the same parser and validation boundary. Bulk
sequence identity updates apply the scalar recurrence to eight bases per iteration and
are locked to the established identity bytes by scalar-alignment and golden tests.

Completed vectors retain normal growth slack unless unused storage is both at least
1 MiB and at least 25% of used storage. Only then is capacity compacted. This avoids an
unconditional full-record copy while still reclaiming unusually large slack.

### BuildSketch and FrozenAxis

An `OphSketch` temporarily stores full 64-bit winners, orientation, HLL, and observation
count. Axis construction hashes each relevant k-mer once into half-bin sketches, then
merges exact register winners into core and expanded cells.

Each axis also owns the complete validated `ScientificConfig` and source-sequence
identity. `FrozenAxis` storage is private; ordinary `TileRequest` values are geometric
only, and tile parameters are derived from compatible axes before allocation.

`AxisOverview::freeze` discards builders and retains only:

* coordinate bounds and sequence metadata;
* register occupancy;
* 32 fingerprint bit planes;
* reverse and ambiguous orientation planes;
* HLL cardinality and observation scalars.

Ordinary browser axes carry no complete k-mer sets. The non-default `validation`
feature can additionally populate bounded sparse-core sets for controlled experiments;
that storage and its correction kernels are outside the production path. Freezing
prevents the previous double retention of full winners plus bit planes.

### MatrixTile

Tiles are row-major arrays with equal dimensions:

* `Uint16 identity`, scaled by 10,000; `65535` is missing;
* `Int16 direction`, scaled to `[-32767,32767]`;
* `Uint16 directionSupport`.

Wasm consumes its Rust vectors when returning channels. wasm-bindgen performs the one
necessary Wasm-to-JavaScript copy, after which the worker transfers ownership to the
main thread without another `.slice()`.

### PrecomputedOverviewArtifact

The bundled default overview uses a versioned binary envelope compressed with
deterministic gzip. Its JSON header identifies the generator, exact FAI text, sequence
metadata, source FASTA/FAI/annotation filenames, byte lengths and SHA-256 values, the
comparison, and complete scientific configuration fields plus the 54-byte canonical
identity encoded as hex. Its binary payload stores the ordinary identity, direction,
and direction-support arrays for every refined tile.

Decoding is defensive: magic, schema, header size, UTF-8/JSON shape, source roles,
hash formats, FAI records, configuration identity/digest agreement, comparison bounds,
tile order, dimensions, channel lengths, non-overlap, and full matrix coverage must all
pass before publication. At worker admission, a newly constructed current
`ScientificConfig` must match the artifact's complete canonical identity and digest.
The digest remains readable provenance; the full identity is the compatibility key.

The checked-in v1 artifact covers the default 1,000-by-1,000 Chr1 self comparison with
`k=21` and 1,024 registers. Its 16 clipped 256-cell tiles contain 1,000,000 cells and
compress from 6,003,800 bytes to 255,582 bytes.

Some static servers infer `Content-Encoding: gzip` from the `.gz` suffix, causing the
Fetch API to expose the 6,003,800-byte decoded envelope even though only 255,582 bytes
crossed the network. The example loader recognizes both exact representations. It
pins and verifies the compressed size/SHA-256 and the decoded size/SHA-256 separately,
then enters the decoder at the matching layer. Arbitrary decompressed or recompressed
content is not accepted.

## 4. Scientific pipeline

The complete estimator is specified in [SCIENTIFIC_SPEC.md](SCIENTIFIC_SPEC.md).
Important implementation properties are:

* matched verified OPH winners divided by union-occupied registers estimates Jaccard;
* 14 low planes prefilter candidate equality, while 32 planes verify the statistic;
* HLL p10 provides cardinality at lower memory than the original p12 candidate;
* both directed containment estimates contribute orientation evidence;
* only the larger directed containment controls displayed identity;
* exact canonical k-mer sets, not production hashes or another estimator, are the
  validation oracle.

The default 85% palette floor is a display decision. The numerical tile retains values
below it, allowing immediate recoloring down to the advanced 80% limit.

## 5. Progressive scheduling

### Bundled example fast path

1. Fetch the 195-byte FAI and approximately 256 KB precomputed overview rather than the
   complete raw genome and annotation. Verify the overview's pinned SHA-256 and require
   the FAI bytes to equal the index embedded in the artifact.
2. Validate its complete structure, source manifest, embedded FAI metadata, tile
   provenance, and exact scientific configuration compatibility with the current Wasm
   engine.
3. Publish all sequence selectors from the embedded FAI and publish the complete
   refined Chr1 default overview directly into the ordinary renderer tile cache.
4. On the first uncached sequence request, represent the same-origin raw FASTA as a
   lazy HTTP-range Blob after a strict two-byte `206 Partial Content` probe. Do not
   consume a `200 OK` full-file response.
5. For a request outside the precomputed/runtime cache, use the ordinary FAI indexed
   path to fetch, validate, pack, and retain only the needed FASTA record range.
6. After the precomputed workspace opens, retrieve and parse the CEN180 annotation in
   a separate job that does not gate the default plot, then attach its one logical row
   to all matching sequences.

Range responses must remain same-origin and have exact `Content-Range` start, end, and
total-size metadata with no content encoding. ETag or Last-Modified is carried through
`If-Range` when available so a changing source cannot silently combine byte ranges.
The fetch adapter retains the active worker global as the receiver for both the probe
and later lazy ranges. This is required by WebKit's brand-checked
`WorkerGlobalScope.fetch` implementation and prevents descriptor-method invocation
from changing the native fetch receiver.
Because startup intentionally does not transfer the full FASTA, it cannot recompute
the artifact manifest's whole-file SHA-256 in the browser. The bundled FASTA, FAI,
and overview are consequently an atomic same-origin deployment unit; release hosts
must update them together, while ETag or Last-Modified protects a live session from
mixing revisions.
Cancellation aborts both the response body and its owning request. Range failure is an
error; it never falls back to an accidental full-genome download.

### Overview

1. Publish validated FAI metadata when a complete index set is present; otherwise
   stream and pack the complete FASTA eagerly. Before a comparison, stream and pack any
   selected indexed records that are not already resident.
2. Build 256-register axes in aligned 256-cell chunks with visible progress.
3. As soon as compatible chunks exist, compute and transfer their quick matrix block.
   Self comparisons expose diagonal and completed off-diagonal blocks incrementally;
   pairwise comparisons expose blocks as each Y chunk joins the completed X chunks.
4. Wait for the renderer's `preview-presented` acknowledgement.
5. Build the 1,024-register detailed axes in aligned chunks and transfer each selected
   detailed block as soon as compatible X/Y chunks exist.
6. Refine tiles whose preview is uncertain around the active display floor or has low
   support, their immediate neighbors, and a deterministic exploratory sample, in
   descending priority order.

Scheduler policy 2 stores 101-bin identity and low-support histograms for each preview
tile before its transferable channels leave the worker. The current palette minimum,
plus or minus five percentage points, defines the active decision region. Immediate
neighbors preserve coherent structure, while a deterministic one-in-sixteen tile
sample prevents a blank preview region from becoming a permanent exclusion rule.
Changing the palette floor updates future selection without recomputing numeric tiles.

Uncertainty is only a display scheduling heuristic. It selects which provisional tiles
receive the detailed estimator and never changes either estimator's numeric result.

### Why quick and detailed builds remain separate

A fine OPH sketch can be projected exactly into a coarser partition. A release-mode
8 Mb/1,000-cell benchmark measured 591 ms for a 2,048-register build plus projection,
versus 672 ms for separate 256 and 2,048 builds. However, projected first paint waited
533 ms instead of 139 ms. The 12% final-time saving did not justify a 3.8-fold first-view
delay, so the interactive path remains quick-first. Projection code and the ignored
benchmark are retained to detect future crossover changes.

### Navigation

The renderer immediately transforms existing lower-resolution tiles during zoom so the
canvas never flashes white. The main thread selects visible 256-cell tiles plus a
one-tile halo. A new request id cancels stale detailed work. Quick tiles for the new
viewport arrive first; detailed refinement begins only after paint acknowledgement.
Exact terminal tiles replace sketches at one base pair per matrix position. They use
complete aligned k-mer footprints. Switching identity/base coloring only redraws
cached textures; Bases is the initial exact visualization.

## 6. State and cancellation

The compute worker uses a serialized promise queue plus owned `DatasetSession`,
`ComparisonJob`, and `FeatureJob` lifetimes. A dataset can serve several later
comparison generations, while each comparison and feature publication must match its
own current immutable identity.

```text
Empty → Loading(staging session) → Ready(committed dataset)
                          │
                          └─ newer load/clear discards staging

Ready → Preparing(request/config) → Serving(preview) → Serving(refined)
                   │                         │
                   └──── newer request cancels stale publication ────┘
```

Load is transactional: files are read into a staging `ComputeSession`; the committed
session changes only after every record succeeds and the operation is still current.
Every dataset-dependent worker message carries a generation. Every tile additionally
carries quality, resolution, coordinates, and configuration digest. The main thread
rejects stale generations even if a browser delivers messages late.

Indexed metadata follows the same generation boundary. Each on-demand record append is
validated against its FAI identifier and length before the global metadata index is
mapped to its local Wasm index. Header validation is deliberately lazy: the real FASTA
header is located within a bounded 256 KiB lookback from the indexed first-base offset,
and its first whitespace-delimited identifier must match the FAI before the parser can
commit the record. FAI-only metadata never gains the optional FASTA description in the
published UI metadata. Failed or cancelled parsing aborts the active FASTA transaction
so the committed records remain usable. Loaded indexed records remain resident until
Clear or dataset replacement and are reused by Self, Pairwise, Grid, feature, and
exact-base requests.

`preview-presented` and cancellation messages bypass queued heavy work so they can take
effect at yield boundaries. Preparation, tile, and annotation-stream loops yield at
bounded shards. Cancelled jobs cannot publish terminal data.

## 7. Cache and memory policy

Memory admission happens before large allocations.

* Wasm zoom-axis cache: 192 MiB.
* Prepared frozen axes: 384 MiB.
* Application-owned Wasm session budget: 3 GiB.
* JavaScript tile cache: 96 MiB.
* GPU textures: 96 MiB.
* Imported annotations: 512 MiB.
* Computed feature tracks: 64 MiB.
* Transient publication: 256 MiB.
* Complete cross-layer plan: 4 GiB.

The Wasm axis cache uses a recency map with logarithmic touch/eviction and tracks
estimated heap bytes. Renderer tile keys include resolution, coordinates, and the
complete configuration digest; quality ranks replacement when a key is shared, and
incompatible tiles cannot alias. Eviction is coordinated back to
the worker so its published-tile bookkeeping cannot grow without bound. The current
overview plus tiles required to avoid a blank viewport are protected, so an unusually
large active viewport can temporarily exceed the renderer's nominal cache budget.

Before risky allocation, the applicable plan selects admission, cache eviction,
quality downgrade, bounded sharding, or rejection with a user-facing fallback. OPFS
spill is reserved but disabled until measurements justify its browser complexity.
Reported memory includes packed sequences, retained Wasm structures, tile CPU arrays,
estimated textures, annotations, and feature tracks. It excludes allocator metadata,
browser internals, and driver overhead. Wasm linear memory can reuse freed regions but
normally does not shrink; reloading the page resets the instance.

The retained sequence heap total is updated when records append, roll back, or clear,
rather than recalculated by walking every record for each status update. Each sequence's
estimate includes retained vector and string capacities, including slack below the
compaction threshold. Indexed records do not contribute packed-sequence memory before
they are loaded, but their small index metadata and browser-owned source `File` objects
remain outside the Rust/Wasm estimate.

## 8. Rendering and recovery

WebGL2 shaders apply the similarity or direction palette without changing numeric
tiles. Similarity uses the selected plot background below the minimum and maps the
chosen palette colors across the minimum/midpoint and midpoint/maximum segments as
discrete display bins. ColorBrewer schemes use their exact published class sets;
Viridis variants are discrete samples from d3-scale-chromatic's published 256-color
table without RGB interpolation. Palette direction reverses the resolved ordered
colors, and editing a swatch replaces that class without changing numeric
tiles. Reversed Spectral is the palette-specific default; other schemes begin in their
canonical direction. Values above the maximum retain the resolved top color. Direction
uses separate forward/reverse hues blended toward equal-luminance gray at low support.
The WebGL clear color is true white. The selected plot background is a tile-shader
input, so a selected black appears only within published tile bounds; empty and loading
plot surfaces remain white. Direction-mode export legends use the same white default.

On `webglcontextlost`, rendering pauses and default loss handling is prevented. On
restore, the program, uniforms, geometry, fallback texture, and every GPU tile texture
are reconstructed from retained CPU arrays. Keyboard controls provide arrow-key pan,
`+/-` zoom, and `Home` reset. The canvas remains focusable and labeled.

Numeric export first checks whether every tile intersecting the current viewport is
already cached at detailed or exact quality. It requests only missing final-quality
coverage, then writes nonzero valid cells as BEDPE by default or as a compact
nine-column scientific CSV. Construction is rejected above two million participating
cells. Calculation metadata stays in the provenance preamble instead of being repeated
in every row. Exact schemas and formulas are defined in
[Data export formats](EXPORT_FORMATS.md).
Image export includes the heatmap, axes, sequence labels, and visible tracks as PNG,
SVG, or PDF. SVG/PDF embed the heatmap as raster while keeping the other components
vectorized. A vector legend occupies a separate right margin so it cannot cover plot
data. For sketch plots, its coordinate axis is linear in ANI_c, while colors are sampled
through the same resolved palette classes, selected color count, and
minimum/midpoint/maximum transfer function as the UI slider and WebGL shader. The
legend uses the same direction and custom colors as the plot. Six evenly spaced ticks
divide the range into five intervals; the adjustable color midpoint does not receive a
special tick, and the palette name is omitted from the legend. Terminal exact plots use
categorical identity, A/C/G/T-base, or orientation keys; all three also distinguish the
background mismatch/below-threshold state from the neutral no-k-mer-evidence state. All
formats carry complete software, method, scheduler, comparison,
scientific-configuration, display, viewport, and sequence provenance.

After the native picker returns, a non-dismissible modal reports export progress and
blocks plot interaction through tile preparation, composition, and file writing. Image
pixels are drawn from cached GPU tiles into an offscreen framebuffer; export neither
resizes nor repaints the visible WebGL canvas. When all visible final-quality tiles are
already cached, no forced-detail worker request is sent.

The browser calls the native system save picker when available, requests Downloads as
its starting directory, and offers format selection inside that picker. Browsers
without this API use an ordinary BEDPE or PNG download. Suggested filenames use
source-qualified, load-unique sequence identifiers; numeric file contents retain the
original FASTA identifiers.

## 9. Security and privacy

The application processes user files locally. A restrictive CSP permits same-origin
scripts/assets, Wasm evaluation, same-origin/blob workers, data images, and local Vite
WebSockets during development; objects and base-URI changes are forbidden. Deployment
must send an equivalent or stricter HTTP header. Automated browser tests fail on
unexpected network egress while processing a fixture.

## 10. Verification pyramid

| Layer | Evidence |
| --- | --- |
| Unit | Parsing, normalization, coordinates, hashing vectors, set operations, UI math |
| Kernel differential | Bit-sliced OPH counters versus test-only scalar comparison |
| Scientific differential | Production score versus exact distinct canonical k-mer containment |
| Statistical/spatial | Multi-realization error, bias, threshold confusion, holes, isolated pixels, continuity, fingerprint events |
| Wasm/browser | Real build, load cancellation, exact entry, transfer semantics, progressive refinement, worker/context recovery, privacy, keyboard |
| Release | Pinned tools/actions, atomic build, SBOM/licenses, separate artifacts, checksums, provenance, biological timing |

Normal CI keeps exact fixtures small and bounded. Chromosome-scale runs measure time and
memory without attempting an exact all-pairs oracle.

## 11. Extension points

### Export

The current export represents the active viewport after every intersecting sketch tile
has been calculated with the selected detailed register count. Terminal-resolution
views use exact k-mer tiles. BEDPE/CSV and complete-composition PNG/SVG/PDF therefore
never publish deliberately provisional quick-view estimates.

### Persistence and 1 Gb operation

Current state is session-local. Robust one-billion-base operation may require sharded
packed sequences, bounded OPFS spill, and a user-visible storage policy. Any persistence
must be opt-in, origin-scoped, versioned, and clearable; it must not weaken the local-only
privacy contract.
